errors.network: We couldn't reach storageGo. Check your connection, then try again.
errors.timeout: storageGo took too long to answer. What you entered is kept; try again.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment, then try again.

errors.codeInvalid: This code doesn't match. Check the latest email we sent and type it again.
errors.codeExpired: This code has expired. Ask for a new one below.
errors.signupExpired: This signup expired after 24 hours without activity. Start again; it takes a minute.
errors.validation: Some details weren't accepted. Check the highlighted fields.
errors.server: Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was lost; try again in a moment.
errors.unknown: Something unexpected happened. Try again; if it keeps happening, contact support.
errors.engine: The encryption engine couldn't start in this browser. Reload the page; if it persists, turn off extensions that block scripts.
errors.selfTest: The encryption engine failed its self-check, so we stopped before using it. Reload the page or try another browser.
errors.crypto: Encryption on this device failed. Nothing was sent. Try again.
errors.invalidCredentials: The email or passphrase doesn't match. Check Caps Lock and the keyboard language.
errors.attemptsLeft: {n} more try before a short pause. | {n} more tries before a short pause.
errors.sessionExpired: Your session ended. Sign in again.
errors.keyChanged: The identity keys stored for your account don't match the ones expected on this device, so nothing was opened. Contact your administrator or storageGo support before signing in again.

auth.offline: You're offline. What you typed is kept; actions resume when the connection is back.
auth.fact: Files are encrypted on your device before they are sent, then stored in Algeria, in line with Law 18-07 on personal data.

fields.name: Full name
fields.emailHint: We'll send a 6-digit code to confirm it.

errors.name: Enter your full name.
errors.emailInvalid: This doesn't look like an email address. Check for typos, e.g. name{'@'}example.dz

start.title: Create your account
start.lead: Files you put in storageGo are encrypted on your device. Only you, and the people you share them with, can open them.
start.orgHint: A company, clinic, firm or administration. You become its first administrator and invite your team.
start.individualHint: A personal account. If you forget your passphrase, only your recovery kit can get you back in.

errors.kind: Choose who the account is for.

org.title: Your organization
org.lead: You'll be its first administrator. You can add other administrators later.
org.nameHint: As your colleagues know you. It appears on invitations.
org.emailHint: Use your work address. We'll send a 6-digit code to confirm it.
org.domainNote: Colleagues whose address ends in {domain} can be invited in one step.

verifyEmail.title: Check your email
verifyEmail.lead: We sent a 6-digit code to {email}. It's valid for 10 minutes.
verifyEmail.resendWait: You can ask for a new code in {time}
verifyEmail.help: Not there? Check your spam folder. Some company mail servers hold messages for a few minutes.

passphrase.title: Choose a passphrase
passphrase.lead: It unlocks your files on every device. We never receive it, so we can't reset it if you forget. That's what keeps your files private, even from us.
passphrase.label: Passphrase
passphrase.hint: At least 4 words or 16 characters. A sentence only you would think of works well.
passphrase.noticeOrg: If you forget it, your recovery kit (next step) gets you back in. Your organization's administrators can also help if organization recovery is on.
passphrase.noticeIndividual: If you forget it, only your recovery kit (next step) can get you back in. No one at storageGo can help, because we never have it.
passphrase.understood: I understand that storageGo can't reset my passphrase.
passphrase.creating: Creating your keys on this device…
passphrase.workKeys: Your keys are created on this device
passphrase.workSave: Only encrypted keys are sent to storageGo
passphrase.details: Argon2id (64 MiB, 3 passes) stretches the passphrase into a master key. HKDF-SHA-256 derives the sign-in key and the account encryption key from it. The X25519 and Ed25519 identity keys are wrapped with AES-256-GCM. The passphrase and the master key never leave this device.
passphrase.unsupportedTitle: This browser can't encrypt on this device
passphrase.unsupported: storageGo needs WebAssembly and Web Workers over HTTPS. Use a recent version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.

errors.weak: Too easy to guess. Use at least 4 words or 16 characters.
errors.understood: Confirm that you understand before continuing.

kit.title: Save your recovery kit
kit.lead: Your recovery kit is the only way back in if you forget your passphrase. Print it or save it somewhere offline, and keep it like a passport.
kit.restoring: Creating a new recovery kit on this device…
kit.facts: {count} words, created on {date}. Write them down, print them or download them.
kit.downloaded: Kit downloaded. Move the file somewhere offline, then delete it from Downloads.
kit.keep1: Anyone with these 24 words can get into your account. Don't send them by email or chat.
kit.keep2: Keep a copy offline: on paper, or on a USB key in a drawer, not in a cloud folder.
kit.keep3Org: If you lose both your passphrase and this kit, only your organization's administrators can restore your access, and only if organization recovery is on.
kit.keep3Individual: If you lose both your passphrase and this kit, no one can recover your files, not even storageGo.
kit.saveFirst: Download or print your kit first

sheet.title: Recovery kit
sheet.how2: Choose “I have my recovery kit” and type these 24 words in order.
sheet.how3: Choose a new passphrase. Your files open again on every device.
sheet.foot: Keep this page private and offline, like a passport. storageGo never has a copy and can't replace it.

kitLost.title: Your recovery kit is no longer on this page
kitLost.body: The page was reloaded, and the kit was never saved anywhere, by design. Your account exists: sign in and a new kit will be created for you here.

keysLocked.title: Your keys are locked
keysLocked.body: The page was reloaded, so the keys created on this device are no longer in memory. Sign in to unlock them and continue here.

leave.title: Leave before confirming your kit?
leave.body: Your account is created, but your recovery kit isn't confirmed yet. If you leave now, you'll need to sign in to create a new one.

verifyKit.title: Check your recovery kit
verifyKit.lead: Type two words from the kit you just saved, reading them from your copy. This proves it's complete and readable.
verifyKit.stuck: Can't find the words? Your copy may be incomplete. Go back and save the kit again.

errors.wrong: This isn't word #{n} of your kit. Check the number and the spelling.

orgRecovery.title: Recovery for {org}
orgRecovery.lead: Lets your administrators restore a member's access when they forget their passphrase and lose their recovery kit.
orgRecovery.fact1: The recovery key is created on this device and stored only in encrypted form. storageGo can't use it.
orgRecovery.fact2: Each recovery is approved by an administrator, who checks the person's identity and re-enters their own passphrase.
orgRecovery.fact3: Without it, a member who loses both their passphrase and their kit loses their files.
orgRecovery.coAdminHint: Recommended: recovery keeps working when you're away. They'll receive an invitation.
orgRecovery.requireTwo: Require two administrators to approve each recovery
orgRecovery.requireTwoHint: Starts once the second administrator joins. Protects against one person being misled.
orgRecovery.requireTwoDisabled: Add a second administrator to turn this on.
orgRecovery.creating: Creating the recovery key on this device…
orgRecovery.doneInvited: Organization recovery is on. Invitation sent to {email}
orgRecovery.inviteFailed: Recovery is on, but the invitation couldn't be sent. {reason} You can invite them from Admin later.
orgRecovery.skipBody: Members who forget their passphrase and lose their kit will lose their files, and no administrator will be able to help. You can turn recovery on later in Admin › Policies.
orgRecovery.skipUnderstood: I understand that lost files can't be restored without it
orgRecovery.details: An X25519 key pair is generated in this browser. Its private key is wrapped to each administrator with HPKE (RFC 9180); with two-administrator approval it is split 2-of-n with Shamir's secret sharing. Your identity keys get an extra copy sealed to its public key.

errors.self: This is your own address. Enter another administrator's.

invite.title: Invite your team
invite.lead: Each person chooses their own passphrase. Files are encrypted for the people they're shared with, not for administrators.
invite.label: Email addresses
invite.hint: Separate addresses with commas, spaces or new lines.
invite.csvImported: {n} address added from {name} | {n} addresses added from {name}
invite.csvTooLarge: This file is larger than 1 MB. Split it, or paste the addresses instead.
invite.csvUnreadable: {name} couldn't be read. Export it again as CSV (UTF-8).
invite.roleHint: Administrators manage members, policies and recovery requests.
invite.later: You can invite people any time from Admin › Members.
invite.skippedTitle: {n} address was not invited | {n} addresses were not invited

errors.invalid: Fix this address: {list} | Fix these addresses: {list}
errors.tooMany: You can invite up to {max} people at a time.

email.title: Sign in
email.lead: Your files open on this device once you enter your passphrase. It never leaves the device.
email.expired: Your session ended. Sign in again to continue where you were.

passphrase.title: Enter your passphrase
passphrase.paused: Too many attempts. You can try again in {time}.
passphrase.keyChangedTitle: We stopped to protect your account
passphrase.details: Argon2id runs on this device and turns the passphrase into a sign-in key; only that key is sent. The server answers with your keys still wrapped, and they are opened here.

approve.title: Approve this sign-in
approve.lead: This browser is new to your account. Approve it from a device where you're already signed in.
approve.step1: On your other device, open storageGo: a sign-in request appears.
approve.step2: Check that it shows the same two words, then approve it.
approve.noDeviceOrg: An administrator of your organization can approve this device instead, or you can use your recovery kit.
approve.noDeviceIndividual: Use your recovery kit to sign in on this device.
approve.adminAsked: Request sent to your administrators. This page continues once one of them approves.
approve.reenter: The page was reloaded while waiting, so enter your passphrase once more to finish.
approve.denied: It was declined on one of your devices. If that wasn't you trying to sign in, there's nothing else to do.
approve.expired: Requests are valid for 10 minutes. Send a new one and approve it on your other device.
approve.renewed: New request sent. It's valid for 10 minutes.
approve.gone: It was replaced by a newer sign-in or cleaned up. Start again to send a new one.

unlock.title: Unlock your files
unlock.lead: You're still signed in, but your keys were cleared from this page's memory. Enter your passphrase to open them again.
unlock.leadIdle: Your files were locked after a period of inactivity. Enter your passphrase to open them again.

signout.title: You're signed out
signout.lead: Your keys were wiped from this device's memory.
signout.done: Your session on this device is closed.
signout.partial: We couldn't reach storageGo to close the session on the server. It will expire on its own; try again to close it now.

app.offline: Offline. Uploads will resume when you're back.

notifications.label: Notifications
notifications.request_upload: New files arrived through a file request
notifications.device: A new device signed in to your account

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.lead: Single-letter shortcuts work when you're not typing in a field.
shortcuts.enabledHint: Turn off if they get in the way of a screen reader or voice control.

reason.unreadable: This item's name and key can't be opened
reason.someViewOnly: Some selected items are view only

list.decrypting: Loading and decrypting names on this device…

drop.unreadable: That folder couldn't be read. Try uploading it with “Upload a folder”.

folder.missing: It may have been deleted, or it's no longer shared with you.

empty.orgWhere: Files are encrypted on each device, then stored in {where}.
empty.folderHint: Drop files here or use Upload. They are encrypted on this device before they're sent.
empty.shared: When a colleague shares a file, it appears here.
empty.recent: Files you upload or change appear here.
empty.starred: Star files and folders to find them here quickly.
empty.trash: Deleted items stay here for 30 days before they're destroyed.
empty.links: Create one from a file's Share menu to send it to someone outside your organization.
empty.requests: A file request lets someone send you files without an account.

shared.note: Files and folders colleagues shared with you.

trash.note: Items are destroyed 30 days after they're moved here, with their keys.

search.note: Search looks at file names only. Contents are encrypted, so they can't be searched.
search.prompt: Type part of a file name. {n} names are ready on this device.
search.none: Search looks at file names in this workspace only. Check the spelling, or try a shorter part of the name.

links.note: Links you created. The key part of a link exists only in the link itself, so it can't be shown again here.

requests.note: Links through which people without an account can send you files.
requests.closed: Request closed. The link no longer accepts files.

details.label: Details
details.none: Select a file or folder to see its details.
details.chunksValue: 256 KiB chunks, each with its own integrity tag
details.copiesValue: {n} (one per person or link with access)
details.notVerified: Not downloaded on this device yet
details.fileNote: This file has its own key, made on the uploader's device. The server stores the key only in wrapped form, so it can't open the file or read its name.
details.folderNote: This folder has its own key, which wraps the keys of what's inside. The server can't open it.
details.versionRestored: The version of {date} is now the current one.
details.activityNote: Activity never includes names or contents: the server doesn't have them.

errors.taken: “{name}” is already used in this folder.

move.title: Move {what}
move.intoItself: A folder can't be moved into itself or one of its own folders.

delete.title: Delete {n} item forever? | Delete {n} items forever?
delete.consequence: This item will be destroyed. Its key is deleted, so not even a backup can open it. | These {n} items will be destroyed. Their keys are deleted, so not even a backup can open them.
delete.confirm: Delete {n} item permanently | Delete {n} items permanently

conflict.title: This name is already used
conflict.keepBothHint: The new file gets a number added to its name.
conflict.replaceHint: It becomes a new version. The current one stays in the version history.
conflict.all: Do the same for the next conflict | Do the same for the next {n} conflicts

share.title: Share “{name}”
share.noMatch: No one in your organization matches.
share.verifyFirst: Confirm you checked the fingerprint first
share.keyChanged: {name} has a new key since you last shared with them. This happens when someone resets their account, but it could also mean someone is trying to intercept. Check the fingerprint above with {name} in person or by phone before sharing.
share.memberKeyChanged: Key changed since this share. Verify before sharing more.
share.recallNote: Removing access doesn't recall copies someone already downloaded.

link.passwordHint: Send it separately from the link, for example by phone.
link.creating: Creating the link key on this device…
link.keyNote: The highlighted part is the key. It never reaches our servers.
link.onceNote: Copy the link now: it can't be shown again.
link.passwordNote: Send the password separately, not in the same message as the link.
link.revoked: Link revoked. People who have it can no longer open the file.
link.blocked: Your organization doesn't allow share links.
link.blockedAsk: Your organization doesn't allow share links. Ask {who} if you need one.

request.title: New file request
request.lead: Anyone with the link can send files into the folder you choose. Their files are encrypted in their browser, and they can't see what's already there.
request.name: Request title
request.nameHint: Shown to the people who use the link.
request.onceNote: Copy the link now: its key part can't be shown again.

quota.fullOrg: Uploads are paused until space is freed or added. Ask {who} to add space, or empty the Trash.
quota.fullPersonal: Uploads are paused until space is freed. Empty the Trash or choose a larger plan.

preview.onDevice: Decrypted on this device. The server never sees the contents.
preview.verifiedHint: Every chunk matched its integrity tag: the file is exactly as it was uploaded.
preview.alteredTitle: This file can't be opened safely
preview.altered: It was altered or damaged after it was uploaded, so it wasn't decrypted. Your other files are not affected.
preview.noAccess: Ask {owner} to share it with you again.
preview.unsupported: This type of file can't be shown here. Download it to open it on your device.
preview.textCut: Only the beginning is shown. Download the file to see all of it.

tray.label: Transfers
tray.paused: Paused: offline. It resumes by itself when you're back.
tray.quota: Storage is full. Free some space, then try again.
tray.quotaOrg: Storage is full. Ask {who} to add space.
tray.access: You no longer have access to this file.
tray.someFailed: {n} transfer needs attention | {n} transfers need attention
tray.note: Files are encrypted on this device before they're sent.

toast.trashed: {what} moved to Trash | {what} moved to Trash
toast.deleted: {n} item deleted forever | {n} items deleted forever
